nodes.description: GnRH neurons originate outside the brain and reach the hypothalamus along olfactory and terminal-nerve axons, which is why reproductive and olfactory deficits travel together in Kallmann syndrome. Tcf12 is expressed at high levels in the embryonic ectoderm and along the olfactory neuron migratory route. In zebrafish, suppressing tcf12 shortens the terminal-nerve axons that GnRH neurons migrate along and reduces olfactory bulb size, in a dose-dependent way. In patients the structural correlate is olfactory bulb hypoplasia on MRI.

nodes.description: Absent or insufficient hypothalamic GnRH input leaves pituitary gonadotropes unstimulated, so LH and FSH are inappropriately low in the face of low sex steroids. The other pituitary axes are intact, which separates this from combined pituitary hormone deficiency. Both TCF12 case reports show a blunted gonadotropin response to exogenous GnRH.

nodes.description: TCF12 is a class I bHLH protein that regulates transcription as a heterodimer with class II bHLH factors. In the coronal suture the relevant partner is TWIST1, and mice heterozygous for both genes develop severe coronal synostosis. Which class II partner matters in the GnRH lineage is not established; the zebrafish work shows reduced expression of tcf3a/b, another E protein, and of stub1 after tcf12 loss.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in TCF12, encoding a basic helix-loop-helix partner of TWIST1, are a frequent cause of coronal craniosynostosis.
evidence.snippet: TCF12 encodes one of three class I E proteins that heterodimerize with class II bHLH proteins such as TWIST1.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in TCF12, encoding a basic helix-loop-helix partner of TWIST1, are a frequent cause of coronal craniosynostosis.
evidence.snippet: mice doubly heterozygous for loss-of-function mutations in Tcf12 and Twist1 have severe coronal synostosis. Hence, the dosage of TCF12-TWIST1 heterodimers is critical for normal coronal suture development.
